_comment: Connection template for the Enterprise Geodatabase. Copy it, fill it in, and pass the
copy with --connection; or pass the individual flags and skip the file entirely.
There is deliberately no password field. It comes from the EGDB_PASSWORD environment
variable or --password, and never from a committed file (CLAUDE.md sections 10 and 11).
The opensearch use case carries a committed throwaway password under the narrow
exception in section 10; that exception is not taken here, because an Enterprise
Geodatabase is not a folder that gets deleted with build/ - it is a database instance
with a real login, and the demo cost of one 'set EGDB_PASSWORD=...' is smaller than the
cost of getting that judgement wrong.
Note what the .sde file the importer generates does contain: ArcGIS Pro can hang when
opening a geodatabase from a connection file whose credentials were not saved, so
import_to_egdb.py creates it with SAVE_USERNAME. That means the generated file carries
the credentials - which is exactly why it is written to build/ and gitignored, never to

_field_notes.instance: The PostgreSQL host. 127.0.0.1 rather than 'localhost' or the machine name, to keep name resolution out of a connection that does not need it. For a non-default port, Esri's documented syntax could not be confirmed on a version-specific page - try 'host,port' and check the result rather than assuming.
_field_notes.database: Required for PostgreSQL, unlike SQL Server where it may be blank. Must be lowercase: PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers, and ArcGIS never quotes them.
_field_notes.username: The data owner - the login that will own the feature class. Not 'sde': the sde login owns the geodatabase system tables, and putting user data in that schema mixes the two.
_field_notes.schema: Null means the user's own schema, which is the normal case for a user-schema geodatabase.
_field_notes.version_type: TRANSACTIONAL is the default. BRANCH would be the choice for a branch-versioned feature service, which this use case does not build.
